title: Robot Deployment Scorecard
intro: What a humanoid stack needs from research before it can be deployed, how far published work has got, and the measures that decide when each piece is good enough. Every metric is measured on the deployment hardware, on a named subtask, with the data budget stated.

areas.name: Force-aware manipulation
areas.biggestGap: Generalizing grip force across many objects before vision shows a cue
areas.goal: A model trained on force and vision together that knows how much force each object needs, split into normal, shear and torsion, and reacts before a visual cue appears.

evidence.text: Tactile-VLA reads normal and shear force and infers grip force for unseen objects; 80–100% success on fragile items against 0–50% for baselines, with 50–100 demos per task.
τ uses gripper tactile sensing without force labels; 71.25% on four contact-rich tasks against 28.75% for π0.5 and 30% for ForceVLA, 100 demos per task, tested on unseen objects.
TaF-VLA aligns tactile signals with a 6-axis force/torque reading inside π0.5; 22% higher average success on seven force-critical tasks.

gaps: Each paper covers 4–7 tasks on a single arm
No on-device control rate reported
No measure of acting before the visual cue
Threads, latches and snap-fits not covered; simulators cannot model them

areas.name: Edge inference near 50 Hz
areas.biggestGap: Small fine-tunable models reacting at control rate on Jetson Thor
areas.goal: A small model that can be fine-tuned per subtask and reacts at about 50 Hz on Jetson Thor, so force readings change the action in time.

evidence.text: Community benchmark on Jetson Thor: π0.5 at 44 ms per inference (about 23 Hz); GR00T N1.6 at 41–45 ms. Not official NVIDIA figures.
Jetson-PI runs π0.5 with asynchronous inference at 7.59 Hz control frequency and 131.8 ms reaction time on Thor.

VLA-HWBench times 19 open VLA configurations on Jetson AGX Thor with a real LIBERO observation: fastest median call X-VLA 76.7 ms, VLA-Adapter 92.7 ms, GR00T N1.7 119 ms, π0.5 405 ms; 10 of 19 keep up with a 20 Hz controller only by playing back action chunks. No physical robot runs; not peer reviewed.

Community benchmark (ZETIC) on Jetson AGX Thor, BF16 batch 1: π0.5 254 ms eager / 132 ms torch.compile at 11.9–12.4 GB and 68–87 W; SmolVLA 50 ms compiled (6.76 GB, 67 W); GR00T N1.7 109 ms eager. π0.5 on AGX Orin 394–949 ms. An NVIDIA reply cites 49 ms for π0.5 with TensorRT FP8+NVFP4. Not robot-validated.

gaps: No VLA shown reacting at 50 Hz on Thor
Action chunking can play actions at 50 Hz while the model only sees new force data at 10–20 Hz
Papers rarely report latency on the deployment device
Thor latency for the same model varies up to about 8× with runtime and precision (π0.5: 405 ms, 254 ms, 132 ms, 44–49 ms across reports), so papers must state runtime, precision and power mode

areas.name: Workspace awareness
areas.biggestGap: Deciding where to stand and when to start a motion
areas.goal: The robot judges whether it can reach or see, moves closer when it cannot (for example to read a sign), and hands off cleanly between navigation, vision and manipulation.

evidence.text: Active Spatial Brain on Unitree G1: a VLM moves the neck and base and a solver computes the base adjustment to reach; 70–85% on easy and 55–70% on hard settings. VLMs struggle with fine metric judgment.
HEAD on Unitree G1: navigation hands over to reaching on a fixed trigger (target in view and in range); 71% overall, 50% in a kitchen.

gaps: When to start a motion is still a hand-set rule
No work on moving closer to read a sign or label
Success drops sharply in cluttered or narrow spaces

metrics.measure: Predicted vs actual reachable; precision and recall
Subtask succeeds without repositioning
Moves when out of reach instead of stretching or failing
Distance from the best manipulation pose
Motion start against first moment conditions held
Walk to reach, squat to stand, without stall or fall
Walks until legible, then reads it correctly
Read text changes the plan correctly
Navigation to vision to manipulation, no person
Repositions and retries after a failed grasp

areas.name: Semantic map navigation
areas.biggestGap: Recognizing places from new viewpoints without metric SLAM
areas.goal: A relative, semantic map of rooms, objects and how places connect, with go-until-condition moves and lidar used only for collision avoidance.

evidence.text: Object-Path Graph on a Jetson wheeled robot: 91% node-transition success, 83% object query, 74–88% relocalization recall@1. It still uses odometry and RGB-D mapping.
GPT-6 Astra reached 92% on RxR instruction following from a single RGB camera, but kept no map and searched inefficiently.

gaps: Viewpoint changes still break place recognition
Not shown on humanoids
No system drops odometry entirely

metrics.measure: ≥3 headings, 2 lighting conditions
Distinct places merged into one node
Smoothed over N frames
"Go to the X" reached
Walk until the stop condition fires
At normal walking speed
Moved object found or reported missing
Time and nodes before first goal reached

areas.name: Clearing obstacles to shorten a path
areas.biggestGap: Deciding to move an object (a chair) instead of detouring
areas.goal: Use semantic cues to decide when moving an object aside beats a longer route, and refuse objects that must not be moved.

evidence.text: A 2026 study classifies obstacles as movable (87% precision) or fixed (81%) and pushes movable ones with an arm; 90% navigation success in a lab, with obstacle runs 19% slower than clear runs. Mobile robot, not a humanoid.

gaps: No humanoid work found
Pushing only; no grasp-and-place
No cost comparison against the detour

metrics.measure: Against a hand-labelled answer
Object moved and path completed
Same start and goal
Fixed, heavy or fragile objects

areas.name: Group conversation by audio
areas.biggestGap: Knowing who is speaking to the robot in a group
areas.goal: Follow who is speaking, respond only when addressed, and turn spoken instructions into the right subtask in site noise.

evidence.text: A 2026 expo field test kept speech recognition near 7% character error in heavy noise, but the authors say the system is not truly multi-party: addressee detection is unresolved and turn-taking used operator commands.

gaps: Addressee detection
Natural turn-taking in groups
Speech recognition fails when people turn away from the microphone

metrics.measure: Site recordings at 1, 3, 5 m, per language
Multi-person recordings with overlap
Was this said to the robot
End of speech to response; p50, p95
Instruction to correct subtask
Audio load while other modules run

areas.name: Whole-body control
areas.biggestGap: Edge cases only; motion triggering moved to workspace awareness
areas.goal: Treated as largely solved by imitation learning from RL policies. Checked for regressions and edge cases, not optimized.

evidence.text: Your assessment: imitation-trained controllers reproduce human motion well enough for deployment. This area was not re-checked against papers.

gaps: Unusual, fast or heavy-contact motions outside the training data
Switching between skills

metrics.measure: Falls and aborts across deployed tasks
Self and environment, minimum clearance logged
Kinematics plus costmap per cycle; p50, p99
Pose error after use; joint-to-scan skew
Slippery floor, payload change, narrow gap

systemMetrics.measure: Per named subtask, no human help, ≥20 trials
Perception, planning, control, force, timing, safety stop
Recovered without help, and time taken
Contacts and emergency stops per subtask
All modules on Thor at once vs each alone
GPU, CPU and memory with everything running
Watts and throttling over repeated subtasks
First demo to validated checkpoint on the robot

testProtocol: Run each test with the model, code version, precision and power mode frozen; the same starts and seeds for every model compared; at least 20 trials per cell with a confidence interval; and every failure labelled by cause.
engineering: Failure triggers: hand-written checks for known failure cases (empty grasp, object not where expected, force over limit, timeout)
Remote takeover when a check fires
Safety around people: slowing, keeping distance, yielding
Speed: tuned against ROI once a reasonable baseline exists from research, for example a subtask in about 2 seconds
notYet: Long-running operation (hours of uptime, failures per hour) until subtasks complete reliably
Simulation evaluation that predicts real results; rigid mechanical contact fidelity is not there yet

changelog.change: Edge inference: added VLA-HWBench (arXiv 2610.34717v2, 27 Oct) Thor latencies for 19 VLA configurations; none reaches a 20 ms call (50 Hz). Maturity unchanged at Early: no robot runs.

Edge inference: added ZETIC community Thor benchmark (28 Oct) with latency, peak memory and power per call for π0.5, SmolVLA and GR00T N1.7, the first source covering the Memory and power metric. Community post, not peer reviewed.
Edge inference: added gap that reported Thor latency for π0.5 spans 44–405 ms depending on runtime and precision, so runtime must be stated for numbers to compare.
Scorecard created from paper reviews (GPT-6 Astra, Devol-ONE) and a search of 2025–2026 work per area.
